schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers
(
    CustomerID INTEGER UNIQUE     not null
        primary key,
    Segment    TEXT null,
    Currency   TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE gasstations
(
    GasStationID INTEGER    UNIQUE   not null
        primary key,
    ChainID      INTEGER          null,
    Country      TEXT null,
    Segment      TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE products
(
    ProductID   INTEGER   UNIQUE      not null
        primary key,
    Description TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE "transactions_1k"
(
    TransactionID INTEGER
        primary key autoincrement,
    Date          DATE,
    Time          TEXT,
    CustomerID    INTEGER,
    CardID        INTEGER,
    GasStationID  INTEGER,
    ProductID     INTEGER,
    Amount        INTEGER,
    Price         REAL
);

CREATE TABLE "yearmonth"
(
    CustomerID  INTEGER not null
        references customers
            on update cascade on delete cascade
        references customers,
    Date        TEXT    not null,
    Consumption REAL,
    primary key (Date, CustomerID)
);
q1: SELECT SUM(IIF(CustomerID = 7, Consumption, 0)) - SUM(IIF(CustomerID = 5, Consumption, 0)) FROM yearmonth WHERE Date = '201304'
q2: SELECT (SELECT Consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 7 AND Date = '201304') - (SELECT Consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 5 AND Date = '201304')
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT SUM(IIF(CustomerID = 7, Consumption, 0)) - SUM(IIF(CustomerID = 5, Consumption, 0)) FROM yearmonth WHERE Date = '201304'
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT (SELECT Consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 7 AND Date = '201304') - (SELECT Consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 5 AND Date = '201304')
counterexample: INSERT INTO customers (CustomerID, Segment, Currency) SELECT 5, 'Consumer', 'USD' UNION ALL SELECT 7, 'Corporate', 'USD'; INSERT INTO yearmonth (CustomerID, Date, Consumption) SELECT 5, '201304', 10 UNION ALL SELECT 7, '201304', 20;
explanation: Q1 calculates the difference in consumption between CustomerID 7 and CustomerID 5 for the specific date '201304', summing up the consumption for each customer and then subtracting. Q2, on the other hand, directly subtracts the consumption of CustomerID 5 from the consumption of CustomerID 7 for the same date, without summing up any values.
counterexample_dsp: The difference arises when the consumption values for CustomerID 7 and CustomerID 5 on '201304' are different. Q1 will sum up the consumption for each customer and then subtract, while Q2 will directly subtract the consumption of CustomerID 5 from CustomerID 7.
